what: The SQL Formatter turns hard-to-read SQL into clean, consistently indented queries. Each clause such as SELECT, FROM, WHERE and GROUP BY starts on its own line, columns and conditions are indented, and keywords can be written in upper or lower case.

It is for developers, data analysts, database administrators and students who read and write SQL: tidy a query copied from a log or an ORM, prepare SQL for code review or documentation, or make a colleague's one-line query understandable.
It understands 20 SQL dialects and works entirely in your browser, so queries with private table names or data stay on your device.
uses: Format long one-line SQL produced by an ORM, BI tool or log file.
Give every query the same style before committing it or adding it to docs.
See the structure of a query clearly, clause by clause.
Spot a missing join condition or a misplaced AND when each part is on its own line.
Compact a query to a single line for logs, scripts or config files.
tutorial: Paste it into Your SQL, open a .sql file, or press Load sample. Several statements separated by semicolons are fine.
Choose your database under SQL dialect so features like [brackets], backticks, $$ strings or special functions are understood.
Keywords sets SELECT or select; Function names sets COUNT or count; Indent picks 2 spaces, 4 spaces or a tab.
Standard indents each clause. Aligned columns lines keywords up in a column on the left or right. AND / OR places logical operators at the start or end of lines.
Tick No spaces around operators for a=b, or Semicolon on its own line.
The result updates as you type. Press Copy SQL or Download .sql. For one line instead, press Compact to one line.
features: From MySQL and PostgreSQL to BigQuery, Snowflake and SQL Server.
Keyword and function case, indent, aligned layouts and operator placement.
Strings, quoted identifiers and comments are never changed.
One-line SQL with comments kept safely.
Shows the line and column where the formatter got stuck.
Formats thousands of statements in a couple of seconds.

example.title: Worked example: a report query
example.text: Press Load sample to get a one-line query that joins customers and orders. With PostgreSQL, UPPER CASE keywords and 2 spaces, the result starts with SELECT on its own line, then c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders and SUM(o.total) AS revenue each on an indented line, followed by FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o, the WHERE conditions with AND at the start of each line, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY revenue DESC and LIMIT 20.

tips: Always choose your real database dialect; Standard SQL is strict and rejects many database-specific features.
Use Aligned columns for short queries in documentation; Standard reads better for long, nested queries.
Keep keywords in UPPER CASE and names in lower case to make queries easy to scan.
Template placeholders like {{name}} or :param may need the right dialect to be recognised.
Compact to one line keeps comments as /* */ so the query still runs.
problems: Could not format with Standard SQL
Choose your database under SQL dialect; Standard SQL does not know names in [brackets], backticks or many functions.
The error points to the end of the query
A bracket or quote is probably not closed. Count the opening and closing parentheses and quotes.
Function names did not change case
Set Function names to UPPER CASE or lower case; Keep as typed leaves them alone.
It does not update while typing
Scripts over about 300,000 characters are formatted only when you press Format SQL.
